title: The Recipe I Improved Too Early
scene: You try a highly rated recipe, decide to improve the sauce before reading the next step, and then discover the recipe was about to add exactly the same ingredients. You follow the rest of the instructions anyway and end up with a meal that is far more intense than intended.
sceneJa: 高評価のレシピを見つけて料理を始めるが、次の手順を読む前にソースへ独自のアレンジを加える。すると、その直後の工程にまったく同じ材料が書かれており、結果として想定以上に味の濃い料理が完成する。

chunks.en: I decided to cook something new
chunks.ja: 何か新しい料理を作ることにしました
夕食に
そしてレシピを見つけました
何百件も高評価がついている
手順は十分簡単そうで
そして珍しく
実際にそろっていました
材料がほとんど
準備の途中で
ソースを味見して
必要だと思いました
もう少し深みが
レシピを信じる代わりに
ニンニクを加え
少し醤油も加え

chunks.en: and something spicy from the back of the fridge.
chunks.ja: 冷蔵庫の奥にあった辛い何かも入れました

chunks.en: The sauce immediately tasted more interesting,
chunks.ja: ソースはすぐに味わい深くなり
私はそれを受け取りました
自分には分かっている証拠として
何をしているのかが

chunks.en: Then I reached the next step
chunks.ja: ところが次の手順へ進むと
レシピには書かれていると分かりました
これから加えるところだったと
ニンニク、醤油、唐辛子を
量を減らすことも考えました
でもそのころには
妙にこだわるようになっていました
自分版の展開に

chunks.en: So I followed the remaining instructions exactly
chunks.ja: そこで残りの手順には正確に従い
料理を完成させました
十分すぎるほど味のある
小規模な非常事態にも耐えられそうな

chunks.ja: かなり革新的な手法を試すかもしれません

アレンジする前に

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: Instead of trusting the recipe / I added some garlic / a little soy sauce / and something spicy from the back of the fridge
Instead of / trusting the recipe I / added some garlic a little / soy sauce and something spicy from the back of the fridge
Instead / of trusting / the recipe I added / some garlic a little soy sauce
questions.explanation: The first version keeps the contrast phrase ‘Instead of trusting the recipe’ together and then groups the ingredients naturally.

questions.question: What does ‘which I took as evidence that I knew what I was doing’ mean?
options: The speaker treated the better taste as proof that the improvisation was correct
The speaker found written evidence in the recipe
The speaker decided to stop cooking
questions.explanation: ‘Take A as evidence that ...’ means interpreting A as proof that something is true. Here the speaker becomes overconfident because the sauce initially tastes better.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence funny?
options: It says recipes should never be changed
It presents simply following the full recipe first as if it were a radical new cooking method
It suggests the meal was impossible to eat
questions.explanation: The dry humour comes from describing the very ordinary idea of finishing the recipe before modifying it as a ‘radical technique’.

speak: Start with mild optimism and confidence. Let ‘Instead of trusting the recipe’ sound like a small decision rather than a dramatic mistake. Give ‘which I took as evidence’ a slightly self-satisfied rhythm, then pause at ‘Then I reached the next step’ to mark the reversal. Read the final sentence very calmly, as if following a recipe before changing it really were an advanced technique.
review: Flow: trusted recipe → early improvisation → false confidence → discovery that the recipe planned the same additions → commitment to the mistake → overly intense meal → dry lesson. Useful chunks: ‘Instead of -ing’, ‘take A as evidence that ...’, and ‘by then’. Notice how the ending does not complain about the food; it treats basic restraint as a sophisticated future strategy.
